newsitem.title: UK: Arbitrage pulls more U.S. gas oil to Europe - trade.
newsitem.headline: Arbitrage pulls more U.S. gas oil to Europe - trade.

text.p: Another 570,000 tonnes of U.S. gas oil is destined to sail for Europe in October to meet the extraordinary high demand for both 0.2 and 0.05 percent sulphur grades, shipbrokers and oil traders said on Friday.

This latest arbitrage follows about 400,000 tonnes of U.S. production which moved to Europe at the end of September, they added. "We are running out of product in Europe, especially from Russia, and this is being partly compensated by arrivals from the states," a trader said.
Russian gas oil exports from Ventspils slumped by 20 percent in September to 507,000 tonnes and the shortfall was continuing into October, shipping sources said.
The U.S. cargoes sent to Europe include heating oil and European diesel, and dealers saw one such diesel cargo sold on Thursday at November IPE +$22 cif Le Havre.
IPE gas oil futures have climbed $40 in the past two weeks to $250 on Friday, making it the highest price distillate market in the world.
European end users were prepared to pay up to $16 per tonne premium to November futures for a cargo of 0.2 percent geating oil delivered in mid-October.
